What Kind of Aftermath Is This?

When symptoms linger after a trip, people too often put everything into the "I'm broken" bucket, which solves nothing. While a professional can be called in to help at any point, self-diagnostics and basic fix strategies may obviate the need for one. Try to find the underlying psychological or physical patterns driving the symptoms:

Recognizing serotonin toxicity

We can use the Hunter criteria, the same checklist clinicians use to diagnose serotonin syndrome. One or more of these patterns makes the diagnosis more likely:

Spontaneous clonus: involuntary rhythmic muscle spasms, with no stimulation needed to set it off, would be one full pattern
Inducible clonus, spasms set off by stretching/flexing a muscle, plus agitation or sweating would be counted as one pattern altogether.
Ocular clonus (rapid involuntary eye movements) plus agitation or sweating, another pattern together.
Another is tremor (shaking) along with hyperreflexia (abnormally brisk reflexes).
Lastly, Hypertonia (muscular rigidity) with fever above 38°C (100.4°F), as well as ocular or inducible clonus.

Anything that could let someone hurt themselves in the next five minutes takes priority, so get the car keys out of reach and turn the stove off, and move them away from roads and balconies, or pools of water for that matter. Letting them move around is fine, and pacing can help, but keep them from taking more of any substance. If they want to go confront somebody, that can wait until tomorrow. And if they want to leave, have someone go with them. Put any weapons away and keep the person away from crowds and strangers. If they want to post their big revelation about the universe, or message an ex, take the phone.

Some say there's no such thing as a bad trip, because it's all a doorway to shadow work. But if you had no intention of doing shadow work, that explanation might have come too late. Other bad trips seem unrelated to shadow work, although any negative experience can lead into it. Samsara, the cycle of ordinary existence, offers no shortage of difficult experiences to process. It still makes sense to reduce the trauma the trip itself is causing, so we can address what was already there.
